title: Yarubid dynasty
capsule: The Ya'rubid dynasty (يعاربة) came to power in 1624 when Nasir bin Murshid was elected imam in Rustaq, unifying Oman's fractious tribes against Portuguese coastal domination. Sultan bin Saif I (r. 1649–1688) completed the Portuguese expulsion, seizing Muscat in 1650 and then storming Fort Jesus at Mombasa after a 33-month siege in 1698, projecting Omani sea power across the western Indian Ocean. The dynasty reached its economic apex under Saif bin Sultan I (r. 1692–1711), who financed extensive irrigation infrastructure and a large ocean-going fleet. A succession dispute after 1711 unleashed civil war; Saif bin Sultan II twice invited Persian forces to intervene, fatally undermining Ya'rubid authority, and Ahmad bin Said al-Busaidi emerged as the new imam in 1744, founding the Busaidi dynasty.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Ya'rubid control of the Omani interior is attested through imamate chronicles and Portuguese and British records; their East African domains are well documented, but precise boundaries of hinterland control are approximate.
